content: Ciclesonide nasal spray is prescribed to alleviate symptoms associated with both seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis. These symptoms may include sneezing, nasal congestion, a runny nose, or nasal itching. Ciclesonide belongs to a class of medications known as corticosteroids, which function by reducing and preventing inflammation in the nasal passages. Ciclesonide is available as a liquid solution intended for nasal administration. It is typically used once daily, with one spray in each nostril. It is important to use the medication at the same time every day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use the medication exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. This medication is strictly for nasal use and should not be swallowed or sprayed into the eyes or directly onto the nasal septum (the wall dividing the nostrils). While ciclesonide helps control rhinitis symptoms, it does not cure the condition. Symptom relief may not be noticeable for 24 to 48 hours after the first dose, and full benefits may take longer to manifest. Continue using the medication even if you feel well, and do not discontinue it without consulting your doctor. Each bottle of ciclesonide nasal spray is designed to deliver 120 sprays after initial priming. The bottle should be discarded after 4 months of use, regardless of whether it still contains liquid. To track this, note the date the bottle is removed from its foil pouch and write it on the provided sticker, which can be placed on the bottle. Additionally, keep count of the number of sprays used and discard the bottle after 120 sprays, even if it is before the 4-month mark. To use the nasal spray, follow these steps: 1. Shake the bottle gently and remove the dust cover. 2. If using the pump for the first time, point it away from your body and press down and release the pump eight times until a fine spray appears. If the pump has not been used for 4 days or more, press it once or until a fine spray is visible. 3. Clear your nostrils by blowing your nose. 4. Close one nostril with your finger. 5. Hold the bottle upright with your forefinger and middle finger on either side of the spray tip, and support the base with your thumb. 6. Tilt your head slightly forward and insert the spray tip into the open nostril. 7. Begin to breathe in through your nose, and while inhaling, press down firmly and quickly on the applicator to release a spray. 8. Repeat the process for the other nostril, unless otherwise directed by your doctor. 9. Wipe the spray tip with a clean tissue and replace the dust cover. Ciclesonide may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before using ciclesonide nasal spray, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to ciclesonide, other nasal corticosteroids (e.g., beclomethasone, budesonide, fluticasone, mometasone, triamcinolone), or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking or have recently taken, especially ketoconazole or oral steroids (e.g., dexamethasone, methylprednisolone, prednisone). Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you for side effects. Inform your doctor if you have a history of tuberculosis, cataracts, glaucoma, untreated infections, nasal sores, or herpes eye infections. Additionally, disclose any recent nasal surgery or injuries. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while using ciclesonide, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are using ciclesonide. If you have been taking oral steroids, your doctor may gradually reduce your steroid dose after starting ciclesonide. During this transition, you may experience worsening of conditions such as asthma, arthritis, or eczema. Notify your doctor if this occurs or if you experience symptoms such as extreme fatigue, muscle weakness, abdominal pain, appetite loss, weight loss, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dizziness, fainting, depression, irritability, or skin darkening. Your body may have a reduced ability to handle stress (e.g., surgery, illness, severe asthma attacks, or injuries) during this period. Consider wearing a medical identification bracelet or carrying a card to alert emergency personnel that you may require steroid treatment in emergencies. Ciclesonide may weaken your immune system, making you more susceptible to infections. Avoid contact with individuals who have contagious illnesses such as chickenpox or measles. If you are exposed to these viruses, inform your doctor immediately. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, maintain your normal diet while using this medication. If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not use a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Ciclesonide may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following minor side effects and they persist or worsen: Headache Nosebleeds Nasal burning or irritation Earache Some side effects may be severe. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of the following: Painful white patches in the nose or throat Flu-like symptoms Vision problems Nasal injuries New or worsening acne Easy bruising Swelling of the face and neck Extreme fatigue Muscle weakness Irregular menstrual periods Hives, rash, or itching Swelling of the face, throat, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs Hoarseness Difficulty breathing or swallowing Wheezing Ciclesonide may slow growth in children. It is unclear whether this affects their final adult height. Discuss the risks with your doctor if this medication is prescribed for your child. Report any unusual side effects to your doctor. Store ciclesonide in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from heat and moisture, and do not freeze it. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In case of accidental ingestion, contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or stops breathing, call 911. Prolonged overuse of ciclesonide may result in symptoms such as facial and neck swelling, new or worsening acne, easy bruising, extreme fatigue, muscle weakness, or irregular menstrual periods. Keep all medical appointments while using this medication. If the spray applicator becomes clogged, remove the dust cap, rinse the applicator and cap with warm water, dry them, and reassemble. Do not use sharp objects to clear the spray hole. Do not share this medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. Ciclesonide is marketed under the brand name Omnaris® Nasal Spray.
